chunks: He said: Abu al-Qasim Ja‘far ibn Muhammad ibn Qawlawyh, may Allah have mercy on him, reported to me from ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh, who reported from ‘Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq al-Nahdi, from Yazid ibn Ishaq, from al-Husayn ibn ‘Atiyyah, that Abu ‘Abdillah Ja‘far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon them both, said:

"Noble virtues are ten. If you are able to have them in you, then do so. For they may be present in a man but not in his son, and in a son but not in his father, and in a slave but not in a free man." It was asked: "What are they, O son of the Messenger of God?"

He said: "Truthful speech, faithfulness in hardship, fulfilling trusts, maintaining family ties, hospitality toward the guest, feeding the beggar, reciprocating good deeds, protecting the neighbor, protecting the companion, and the foremost of them all is modesty."

key_terms.التذمم: Protecting honor, fulfilling the rights of protection
key_terms.الحياء: Modesty, bashfulness — considered the head of all virtues
key_terms.المكارم: Noble virtues, excellent character traits (makarim al-akhlaq)
key_terms.صلة الرحم: Maintaining kinship ties, an essential Islamic social obligation

ai.seo_question: What are the ten noble virtues in Islam according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam Ja‘far al-Sadiq (AS) teaches that noble character consists of ten traits that are not inherited by birth or determined by social status, but are acquired through personal effort. These include truthfulness, courage in adversity, trustworthiness, maintaining kinship, hospitality, generosity to the needy, gratitude, protecting neighbors and friends, with modesty (haya) being their crown. This teaching was delivered in the context of an Islamic ethical tradition that valued moral character above social standing.
